name: wlc_phy_rc_sweep_nphy
prose: Static helper of brcmsmac (phy_n.c:27065-27302; the slice cut the head) that calibrates the RX low-pass-filter RC value of an N-PHY radio 2056 core and returns the result as a u8. If pi->pubpi.phy_rev is 7 or greater it returns 0 at once without touching any register. Otherwise it selects tone, bandwidth and target power ratio by whether the channel is 40 MHz, picks the RX/TX radio register offsets from core_idx and loopback_type, saves the TXLPF RCCAL and RXLPF RCCAL_HPC radio registers, the DC-bypass bit (phy 0x48 bit 8), the RX strain-filter registers 0x267-0x270 and the rfctrl override, aux and rssi registers (0xe7, 0xec, 0xf8, 0xfa, and 0x7a or 0x7d), and programs fixed values for the sweep. It then does a binary-style search of the RXLPF_RCCAL_LPC value starting at 128+16: on the first iteration it plays a reference tone (wlc_phy_tx_tone_nphy, result ignored) and measures its I/Q power, then plays the target-bandwidth tone, and each iteration measures I/Q power, forms a power ratio and steps the value up or down, finishing with a final comparison between the last two candidates. The best value is reset to 138 (40 MHz) or 140 (20 MHz) if it lies outside 135..140 (40 MHz) or 137..142 (20 MHz); it is not clamped to the nearest limit. That value is written to RADIO_2056_RX_RXLPF_RCCAL_LPC. It then stops playback, restores all saved radio and PHY registers, sets pi->nphy_anarxlpf_adjusted to false and returns best_rccal_val - 0x80.

name: qm_shr16
prose: Arithmetic shift helper in brcmsmac phy_qmath.c (lines 147-150): it returns qm_shl16(op, -shift). qm_shl16 clamps its shift argument to the range -15..15 and, for a positive shift, doubles the value that many times with saturating 16-bit addition (qm_add16 limits to the s16 range), while for a negative shift it does an arithmetic right shift. So qm_shr16 with a positive shift arithmetically right-shifts op (by at most 15), with a negative shift it left-shifts op with saturation (by at most 15), and with 0 it returns op. If shift is INT_MIN the negation -shift overflows (undefined behaviour in C), which a caller must avoid. It has no side effects.

name: ipw2100_pci_init_one
prose: PCI probe of the ipw2100 driver (real name ipw2100_pci_init_one, ipw2100.c:6125-6322; the listed name ipw2100_pci_probe_one does not exist). It returns -ENODEV, with nothing to undo, if BAR 0 is not a memory resource. It maps BAR 0 (failure: -EIO through the fail label), allocates the net_device with ipw2100_alloc_device (failure: -ENOMEM via fail), enables the PCI device (on failure it frees the libipw device, unmaps and returns the error directly), sets bus master and drvdata, sets a 32-bit DMA mask, requests the regions, adjusts the PCI config retry-timeout byte, checks the adapter is present (-ENODEV), disables interrupts, allocates and initialises the queues (-ENOMEM on allocation failure), requests the shared IRQ, calls ipw2100_up and ipw2100_wdev_init (registered = 1 afterwards) and register_netdev (registered = 2); each failure returns its errno through fail. It then locks priv->action_mutex, creates the sysfs group and, if the RF-kill bit is clear, enables the adapter (failure: stop the adapter, -EIO) and starts a scan; it sets STATUS_INITIALIZED, unlocks the mutex and returns err (0 when everything succeeded). Failures after the mutex was taken go through fail_unlock, which unlocks it. The fail label, if dev is non-NULL, unregisters the netdev when registered >= 2, unregisters the wiphy and frees the band channels when registered is non-zero, stops the adapter, disables interrupts, frees the IRQ if dev->irq is set, kills works, frees the queues, removes the sysfs group and frees the libipw device; regardless of dev it then unmaps the I/O memory, calls pci_release_regions and pci_disable_device (also when the regions were never requested or the device never enabled, for example after a failed ioremap or device allocation) and returns the error.

name: il3945_tx_skb
prose: Queues one frame for transmission on the iwl3945 device (3945-mac.c:444-635; the slice cut the head). It takes il->lock (spin_lock_irqsave) at entry. If RF-kill is active or the frame's tx rate is IL_INVALID_RATE it releases the lock and returns -1 (drop_unlock). Otherwise it releases the lock, looks up the station id (-1 and no enqueue if it is IL_INVALID_STATION), for QoS data frames extracts the TID (-1 if it is >= MAX_TID_COUNT) and returns -1 if the queue space is below high_mark; none of these drops frees the skb. It then retakes il->lock, stores skb in txq->skbs[q->write_ptr], builds the Tx command in the command buffer slot (copies the MAC header, builds crypto, basic and rate fields), DMA-maps the command + MAC header and, when there is a payload, the payload; a mapping failure goes to drop_unlock, releasing the lock and returning -1 without advancing q->write_ptr (txq->skbs[write_ptr] still holds the skb and a mapping that already succeeded is not unmapped here). On success it attaches the buffers to the TFD, records the mapping in the command meta, sets need_update (or wait_write_ptr for fragments with more-fragments set), updates statistics, advances q->write_ptr, updates the device write pointer, releases the lock and, if the queue space is then below high_mark and il->mac80211_registered is set, updates the write pointer again under the lock when wait_write_ptr was set and stops the queue with il_stop_queue; it returns 0.

name: il3945_rs_get_rate
prose: Rate-control callback of iwl3945 that picks the TX rate for one frame (3945-rs.c:604-800; returns nothing; the slice cut the head). rs_sta (il_sta) must be non-NULL: if rs_sta->il is NULL the code only sets its local il_sta = NULL and keeps using rs_sta. It derives the supported-rate mask from the station and band (shifted for 5 GHz) and the user's maximum rate index, starts from idx = min(rs_sta->last_txrate_idx & 0xffff, RATE_COUNT_3945 - 1), and under rs_sta->lock lowers idx to rs_sta->start_rate if that is lower than idx and in the mask (clearing start_rate to RATE_INVALID whenever it was set) and then to the user's maximum rate if that is lower and in the mask. If the window of the resulting idx has fewer than RATE_MIN_FAILURE_TH failures and fewer than RATE_MIN_SUCCESS_TH successes it releases the lock, sets that window's average_tpt to IL_INVALID_VALUE and goes to the common exit with idx unchanged from that point (it may therefore already be start_rate or the user maximum, not necessarily last_txrate_idx). Otherwise it reads the window's throughput and those of the adjacent lower and higher rates allowed by the mask (higher rate disallowed above the user maximum), releases the lock, decides to decrease, keep or increase based on success_ratio against RATE_DECREASE_TH / RATE_INCREASE_TH and the throughput comparisons, cancels a decrease if the success ratio exceeds RATE_HIGH_TH or the throughput exceeds 100 * expected_tpt[low], and moves idx to the lower or higher rate when one exists. At the exit, for 5 GHz it clamps idx up to IL_FIRST_OFDM_RATE (WARN_ON_ONCE), stores idx in rs_sta->last_txrate_idx and sets info->control.rates[0].idx to idx - IL_FIRST_OFDM_RATE; for 2.4 GHz it stores idx in both; it sets rates[0].count to 1. The lock is released before the exit on both paths.

name: __il4965_up
prose: Brings the iwl4965 device up (4965-mac.c:5503-5603; static; the slice cut the head; the caller provides any required locking). It returns -EIO, allocating nothing, if S_EXIT_PENDING is set or if il->ucode_data_backup.v_addr or il->ucode_data.v_addr is NULL. It allocates the broadcast station (a non-zero error is returned after il_dealloc_bcast_stations), calls il4965_prepare_card_hw and returns -EIO after deallocating the broadcast stations if il->hw_ready is false. If the CSR_GP_CNTRL HW_RF_KILL_SW bit is clear it sets S_RFKILL, tells wiphy the hardware rfkill state is true, deallocates the broadcast stations, enables the rfkill interrupt and returns 0. Otherwise it clears S_RFKILL, clears CSR_INT, sets il->cmd_queue to IL_DEFAULT_CMD_QUEUE_NUM, calls il4965_hw_nic_init (a non-zero error is returned after deallocating the broadcast stations), clears the rfkill handshake bits, clears CSR_INT again and enables interrupts, and copies il->ucode_data into il->ucode_data_backup. It then loops up to MAX_HW_RESTARTS times calling il->ops->load_ucode; a load_ucode error is logged and the loop continues with the next attempt (it is not returned immediately); on the first success it calls il4965_nic_start (which returns nothing) and returns 0, leaving the broadcast station allocated. If every attempt fails it sets S_EXIT_PENDING, calls __il4965_down, clears S_EXIT_PENDING and returns -EIO.

name: il4965_rs_move_legacy_other
prose: Chooses the next rate-scaling search table while on a legacy (non-HT) rate (real name il4965_rs_move_legacy_other, 4965-rs.c:1252-1366; the listed name il4965_rs_move_legacy_to_other does not exist; static, returns int). It first sets tbl->action (the active table's action) to IL_LEGACY_SWITCH_SISO and remembers it as start_action, then loops over the actions starting there; each loop pass increments lq_sta->action_counter. ANTENNA1/ANTENNA2: skipped if the number of TX chains is too small or the window success_ratio is at least IL_RS_GOOD_RATIO; otherwise it copies the table into search_tbl, toggles the antenna in search_tbl and, if that succeeds, marks update_search_tbl_counter, sets the expected throughput table and finishes. SISO: copies the table, clears is_SGI and calls il4965_rs_switch_to_siso; on success (return 0) it resets lq_sta->action_counter to 0 and finishes. MIMO2_AB/AC/BC: copies the table, clears is_SGI, sets the antenna pair, skips if that pair is not valid, else calls il4965_rs_switch_to_mimo2 and on success resets action_counter to 0 and finishes. An unsuccessful action advances tbl->action by one (wrapping from MIMO2_BC to ANTENNA1) and the loop ends when it returns to start_action. When finishing after a success it sets lq_sta->search_better_tbl = 1, advances tbl->action by one with the same wrap, and sets search_tbl->action to that value only on the antenna path. If no action succeeded it sets search_tbl->lq_type = LQ_NONE (tbl->action is back at SISO and search_better_tbl is unchanged). It returns 0 on every path; search_tbl may have been overwritten by the attempts either way.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers (name not in slice); real function il4965_rs_move_legacy_other

name: il4965_rs_rate_scale_perform
prose: Core of the iwl4965 rate-scaling algorithm for one transmitted frame (real name il4965_rs_rate_scale_perform, 4965-rs.c:1719-2109; static, returns nothing; the listed name il4965_rs_rate_scale does not exist). It returns at once, changing nothing, if the frame is not a data frame or has NO_ACK. It records lq_sta->supp_rates, updates the traffic-load record and sets lq_sta->is_agg from the TID's aggregation state, selects the active table (or the other one while search_better_tbl is set), sets lq_sta->is_green, and computes the usable rate mask. It returns early, without updating last_txrate_idx, if the current rate index is not in the mask (after logging; if a search was in progress it marks the search table LQ_NONE, clears search_better_tbl and reprograms the uCode with the active table's current rate) or if tbl->expected_tpt is NULL. If lq_sta->max_rate_idx is set and lower than the current index it forces that index and goes to the table update. If the window of the current rate has too little history (fewer than RATE_MIN_FAILURE_TH failures and fewer than RATE_MIN_SUCCESS_TH successes) it marks its average_tpt invalid, calls il4965_rs_stay_in_table and goes to the exit. Otherwise, if a better modulation mode was being searched it compares window throughput with lq_sta->last_tpt: better means the search table becomes active (and enable_counter is set for HT modes); otherwise the search table is marked LQ_NONE, the active table's rate is restored and the uCode table is updated; either way search_better_tbl is cleared and the later search is skipped. If not searching, it compares the throughput of the current and adjacent rates and success ratio to decide to decrease, keep or increase the rate (with a sanity check that cancels a decrease when success is good) and updates the uCode rate table if the index changed. After lq_update it calls il4965_rs_stay_in_table, and, unless the rate changed, a search just finished or staying in the table is set, and the window has counted packets, it saves last_tpt and calls the legacy, SISO or MIMO2 'move_to_other' helper; if that selects a search table it clears that table's history and sends a new link-quality command. It may then set the stay-in-table state (legacy without HT after enough actions, or HT after all actions, also starting aggregation for a high-throughput TID). At the exit it stores the current rate in tbl->current_rate and the index in lq_sta->last_txrate_idx. It acquires no locks.

name: iwl_op_mode_dvm_start
prose: op_mode start callback of iwlwifi's dvm driver (main.c:1233-1524; the slice cut the head). It allocates the ieee80211_hw with iwl_alloc_all (NULL: returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM), nothing to free), stores trans, dev, cfg and fw in priv, selects priv->lib from trans->mac_cfg->device_family (an unsupported family leaves it NULL; WARN_ON then returns ERR_PTR(-ENODEV) after only ieee80211_free_hw). It fills the transport configuration (no-reclaim command list, rx buffer size from the amsdu_size parameter, command groups, cmd FIFO, cb data offset, command queue and key limits depending on the PAN ucode flag, rx MPDU command and header size), calls iwl_trans_op_mode_enter, sets up locks, starts the hardware (iwl_trans_start_hw), reads the EEPROM (iwl_read_eeprom), stops the device, parses the NVM data (-ENOMEM if NULL), checks the NVM version, initialises the hw params, copies the MAC address (a second address with the last byte incremented if more than one is available), sets hw params, adjusts the command queue if the EEPROM disables PAN, initialises queue maps, calls iwl_init_drv, iwl_setup_deferred_work, sets up rx handlers, power and thermal throttling, firmware version string and contexts, calls iwlagn_mac_setup_register and registers debugfs; on success it returns op_mode. On failure it returns ERR_PTR(err) with unwinding by label: iwlagn_mac_setup_register failure runs out_destroy_workqueue (iwl_tt_exit, cancel deferred work, destroy the workqueue) then the labels below; iwl_setup_deferred_work failure starts at out_uninit_drv (iwl_uninit_drv); iwl_init_drv, iwl_nvm_check_version and iwl_eeprom_init_hw_params failures start at out_free_eeprom (kfree priv->nvm_data then priv->eeprom_blob); an iwl_parse_eeprom_data failure starts at out_free_eeprom_blob (frees only the blob); iwl_trans_start_hw and iwl_read_eeprom failures go to out_leave_trans and so skip freeing nvm_data and eeprom_blob (neither is allocated at that point, but the blob pointer may be set by a partial iwl_read_eeprom); every path from there on calls iwl_trans_op_mode_leave and ieee80211_free_hw.

name: rs_move_mimo2_to_other
prose: Chooses the next rate-scaling search table while on a MIMO2 rate in iwlwifi dvm (rs.c:1716-1879; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). First it may force the active table's action to IWL_MIMO2_SWITCH_SISO_A: for a HIGH or CONTINUOUS BT traffic load, for LOW load when the action is SISO_B or SISO_C, when iwl_tx_ant_restriction is IWL_ANT_OK_SINGLE and the action is not a SISO one, and when bt_full_concurrent is set and the action is not a SISO one. It then loops from that action (start_action); every pass increments lq_sta->action_counter. ANTENNA1/ANTENNA2: skipped if tx_chains_num <= 2 or the window success_ratio is at least IWL_RS_GOOD_RATIO; otherwise copies the table to search_tbl and calls rs_toggle_antenna, which returns non-zero on success (then update_search_tbl_counter is set and the loop finishes). SISO_A/B/C: copies the table, sets ant_type ANT_A/B/C, skips an invalid antenna, and calls rs_switch_to_siso, finishing if it returns 0. GI: skipped if the peer does not support short GI at the current width; otherwise copies the table with is_SGI toggled, sets the expected throughput table, skips if the table already uses SGI and last_tpt / 100 reaches the expected throughput, else sets the new current_rate, marks update_search_tbl_counter and finishes. MIMO3_ABC: copies the table, sets ANT_ABC, skips an invalid antenna and calls rs_switch_to_mimo3, finishing if it returns 0 (rs_switch_to_mimo2 is not called here). An unsuccessful action advances tbl->action with wrap from MIMO3_ABC to ANTENNA1 and the loop ends when it is back at start_action, after which search_tbl->lq_type = LQ_NONE. On success it sets lq_sta->search_better_tbl = 1, advances tbl->action with the same wrap and, only if the antenna or GI path was taken, copies the new action to search_tbl->action.

name: rs_rate_scale_perform
prose: Core of the iwlwifi dvm rate-scaling algorithm for one transmitted frame (real name rs_rate_scale_perform, dvm/rs.c:2157-2591; static, returns nothing; the listed name rs_rate_scale does not exist). It returns at once, changing nothing, for non-data frames and NO_ACK frames. It records supp_rates, updates the traffic-load record and lq_sta->is_agg, selects the active table (or the other one while search_better_tbl is set), sets lq_sta->is_green and computes the usable rate mask. It returns early, without updating last_txrate_idx, if the current index is not in the mask (after reverting an in-progress search by setting the search table to LQ_NONE, clearing search_better_tbl and reprogramming the active table's rate) or if tbl->expected_tpt is NULL. A user max rate lower than the current index forces that index and goes to the table update. With too little history in the current window it invalidates the average throughput, calls rs_stay_in_table(lq_sta, false) and goes to the exit. When a search is in progress and iwl_tx_ant_restriction is IWL_ANT_OK_MULTI it adopts the search table if its throughput beats last_tpt (setting enable_counter for HT modes) or reverts to the active table and marks the uCode update needed, clears search_better_tbl and skips mode switching. Otherwise it looks at the throughputs of the adjacent rates to choose decrease, keep or increase, forces a decrease for HT modes when HT is disabled and for MIMO modes when the antenna restriction is not MULTI, applies BT-coex handling (with high BT traffic on MIMO it may force a decrease and call rs_stay_in_table(lq_sta, true), skipping the rate change) and updates last_bt_traffic. It programs the uCode rate table if the index changed, calls rs_stay_in_table when the restriction is MULTI, and, if the rate did not change, no search just ended, the table is not pinned and the window has counted packets, saves last_tpt, calls the legacy, SISO, MIMO2 or MIMO3 move-to-other helper and, if a search table was chosen, clears its history and sends a new link-quality command. It may then set the stay-in-table state and start TID aggregation. At the exit it stores the current rate in tbl->current_rate and the index in lq_sta->last_txrate_idx. It acquires no locks.

name: iwlagn_rxon_connect
prose: Applies an associated RXON configuration for one iwlwifi dvm context (rxon.c:440-507; static; the caller holds priv->mutex; the slice cut the head). For the BSS context it first sends the RXON timing command and returns its error if it fails. It then calls iwlagn_update_qos (result not checked), and for an AP interface sends the beacon with iwlagn_update_beacon, returning its error on failure. All of these failures leave ctx->active unchanged. It then clears priv->start_calib and sends the RXON command from ctx->staging; if that fails it returns the error with ctx->active unchanged but priv->start_calib already cleared. On success it copies ctx->staging into ctx->active, sends the beacon for an IBSS (ADHOC) interface (a failure is only logged), calls iwl_init_sensitivity, and calls iwl_set_tx_power(priv, priv->tx_power_next, true); if that fails it returns the error although the active configuration and start_calib were already updated. It returns 0 when everything succeeded.

name: iwl_advance_tt_handler
prose: Advances the thermal-throttling state machine for a temperature reading (dvm/tt.c:335-456; static; returns nothing; the slice cut the head). It saves old_state = tt->state and scans the (IWL_TI_STATE_MAX - 1) transaction entries of the table for old_state, taking the first with tt_low <= temp <= tt_high; under CONFIG_IWLWIFI_DEBUG a match also logs a large temperature rise and records temp in tt_previous_temp (nothing is recorded when no entry matches or when the option is off), and if that entry's next_state differs from old_state it sets tt->state to it and marks the state changed. Whether or not anything changed, it then calls timer_delete_sync on ct_kill_waiting_tm. If the state changed: for a new state of IWL_TI_1 or higher it sets tt->tt_power_mode to IWL_POWER_INDEX_5 and either clears the HT channel-mode and protection RXON flags in every context's staging RXON (if HT is disabled) or calls iwl_set_rxon_ht(priv, &priv->current_ht_config); for a lower state (IWL_TI_0) it only calls iwl_set_rxon_ht (tt_power_mode is not set). It then takes priv->mutex, clears STATUS_CT_KILL if old_state was IWL_TI_CT_KILL, and if the new state is not IWL_TI_CT_KILL and iwl_power_update_mode(priv, true) fails it logs an error, restores STATUS_CT_KILL if old_state was CT_KILL and restores tt->state to old_state. Otherwise it logs the new state and, on entering CT_KILL from another state, with force true sets STATUS_CT_KILL and calls iwl_perform_ct_kill_task(priv, true), with force false sets tt->state back to old_state and calls iwl_prepare_ct_kill_task; on leaving CT_KILL it calls iwl_perform_ct_kill_task(priv, false). It releases the mutex before returning.

name: TRACE_EVENT(iwlwifi_dev_hcmd,
prose: Tracepoint definition for iwlwifi_dev_hcmd(dev, cmd, total_size, hdr) in iwl-devtrace-iwlwifi.h; the TRACE_EVENT macro generates the function trace_iwlwifi_dev_hcmd. When the event is recorded, TP_fast_assign stores the device name, cmd->flags and a total_size-byte dynamic array holding a copy of the command header (the wide header if hdr->group_id is non-zero, otherwise the plain header) followed by the bytes of every non-empty cmd->data[i] (i below IWL_MAX_CMD_TBS_PER_TFD) in order; hdr and each cmd->data[i] must be readable for the copied lengths, and total_size must cover them or the copy overruns the array. name: iwl_parse_tlv_firmware
prose: Parses a TLV-format iwlwifi firmware image into drv->fw, *pieces and *capa (iwl-drv.c:788-1465; the slice is only a fragment from its NUM_OF_CPU case, the enclosing function being iwl_parse_tlv_firmware(drv, ucode_raw, pieces, capa, usniffer_images)). It returns -EINVAL if the image is shorter than the header or the magic is not IWL_TLV_UCODE_MAGIC (logged). It then records the ucode version, the human-readable string and builds drv->fw.fw_version, and walks the TLVs while at least a TLV header remains: -EINVAL if a TLV's length (or its 4-byte aligned length) exceeds the remaining data, otherwise it dispatches on the TLV type: the instruction/data/boot/sec images and wowlan/usniffer pieces are stored in *pieces, scalar capability TLVs (probe length, PAN, flags, API/capability bitmaps, log pointers and sizes, calibration sizes, PHY SKU, scan channels, station/link/beacon counts, debug addresses) are copied into capa or drv->fw after checking the expected size (a wrong size jumps to invalid_tlv_len, which logs and returns -EINVAL, as do tlv_error cases such as bad DEF_CALIB or out-of-range station/link counts); the NUM_OF_CPU TLV marks the images dual-CPU when it equals 2 and returns -EINVAL for a value outside 1..2; debug destination/config/trigger, memory-segment, IML, recovery info, command-version, PHY integration version, current-PC and PNVM TLVs are copied with allocations whose failure returns -ENOMEM (a duplicate PHY integration string or existing PNVM data is ignored); unknown TLV types are only logged. After the loop it returns -EINVAL if a usniffer image was requested but is not present (and the unified usniffer capability is not set) or if bytes remain after parsing, otherwise 0. Output structures may be partly filled when it returns an error.

name: iwl_mld_rx_monitor_no_data
prose: Handles an RX_NO_DATA notification from the iwlwifi MLD firmware for monitor mode (real name iwl_mld_rx_monitor_no_data(mld, napi, pkt, queue), mld/rx.c:2034-2147; returns nothing; the listed name iwl_mld_rx_no_data does not exist). It returns without doing anything if mld->fw_status.in_hw_restart is set, or (via IWL_FW_CHECK, which logs) if the packet payload is smaller than struct iwl_rx_no_data_ver_3. Otherwise it extracts the channel and chain energies from the descriptor's rssi field, builds a phy_data (phy info words, GP2 on-air rise time, rate_n_flags converted from the v2/v3 rate, with_data false, a copy of rx_vec), and allocates a 128-byte skb with alloc_skb(GFP_ATOMIC); on failure it logs and returns, with nothing delivered. It sets RX_FLAG_NO_PSDU, adds RX_FLAG_FAILED_PLCP_CRC when the descriptor's error field is not RX_NO_DATA_INFO_ERR_NONE, sets zero_length_psdu_type to SOUNDING for NDP, NOT_CAPTURED for MU/TB unmatched and VENDOR otherwise, sets the band (5 GHz if channel > 14, else 2.4 GHz) and frequency, calls iwl_mld_rx_fill_status with link id -1 and a NULL header, sets the mac header at skb->len, and overrides rx_status->nss from rx_vec for VHT, HE and EHT modulation (for other formats nss is left as filled). It then calls ieee80211_rx_napi under rcu_read_lock, which takes ownership of the skb.

name: iwl_mvm_pre_channel_switch
prose: Prepares for a channel switch announcement on a vif in iwlwifi MVM (mvm/mac80211.c:5502-5620; static; the caller holds mvm->mutex; the slice cut the head). It clears mvmvif->csa_failed and csa_blocks_tx and, per vif type: AP: returns -EBUSY (WARN_ONCE) if another CSA is active on mvm->csa_vif, -EBUSY if mvm->csa_tx_blocked_vif is set, then assigns mvm->csa_vif = vif, returns -EBUSY (WARN_ONCE) if mvmvif->csa_countdown is still set (csa_vif stays assigned), records csa_target_freq and, only when chsw->block_tx is set and the hardware has HANDLES_QUIET_CSA, sets csa_blocks_tx, the STOP_AP_CSA state bit on the vif's txq and stops the other stations' TX queues. Station: sets csa_blocks_tx = chsw->block_tx first; if the firmware supports the CHANNEL_SWITCH_ERROR_NOTIF flow it breaks out and skips the rest; otherwise returns -EBUSY if not associated or no DTIM period, may schedule csa_work, runs iwl_mvm_old_pre_chan_sw_sta (its error returned) or iwl_mvm_schedule_client_csa depending on the CHANNEL_SWITCH_CMD capability, and then sets csa_count and clears csa_misbehave. Other vif types do nothing. For every case that reached this point it sets mvmvif->ps_disabled = true, calls iwl_mvm_power_update_ps (a non-zero error is returned with the earlier state left committed) and tears down TDLS peers. It returns 0 on success; earlier changes (cleared flags, csa_vif, csa_blocks_tx, scheduled csa_work, ps_disabled) are not rolled back on the error returns.

name: iwl_mvm_mld_change_vif_links
prose: mac80211 change_vif_links callback of iwlwifi MVM in MLD mode (mld-mac80211.c:1030-1120; static; the slice cut the head). With removed = old_links & ~new_links and added = new_links & ~old_links, it first allocates (kzalloc) and initialises a temporary iwl_mvm_vif_link_info for every added link, unless IWL_MVM_STATUS_IN_HW_RESTART is set, in which case none is allocated; an allocation failure goes to free with -ENOMEM before mvm->mutex is taken. It then takes mvm->mutex. If old_links is 0 and not in HW restart it disables the default link (iwl_mvm_disable_link on vif->bss_conf, an error goes to out_err) and clears mvmvif->link[0]. For each removed link it disables it with the old bss_conf (error: out_err) and frees and clears mvmvif->link[i]. For each added link it gets the link_conf; if it is NULL it issues WARN_ON and skips that link (its temporary allocation is then freed at the end, not stored); otherwise, unless in HW restart, it stores the allocation in mvmvif->link[i], clears the temporary pointer and calls iwl_mvm_add_link (error: out_err). If it got through the loop with new_links == 0 it points link[0] at mvmvif->deflink, adds the default link and sets primary_link = 0 on success (the add's error becomes the result); otherwise, if the primary link is not in new_links, it sets primary_link to the lowest new link. out_err releases mvm->mutex (no rollback on error) and the common tail frees every temporary allocation still held; it returns err, which is 0 on success, -ENOMEM, or the first error from iwl_mvm_disable_link or iwl_mvm_add_link. On error, firmware state and mvmvif->link[] may reflect only part of the change.

name: rs_rate_scale_perform
prose: Core of the iwlwifi MVM rate-scaling algorithm for one station (real body mvm/rs.c:2052-2332; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). It sets lq_sta->is_agg from mvmsta->agg_tids and selects the active table (or the search table while search_better_tbl is set); if aggregation changed it resets the expected throughput table and clears that table's windows. If the current rate index is not in the supported mask it logs an error and returns; before returning, if a search was in progress, it marks the search table's rate LQ_NONE, clears search_better_tbl and reprograms the uCode rate table from the active table. It also returns if tbl->expected_tpt is NULL. With too little history in the current window (fewer than the failure and success thresholds) it invalidates the window's average_tpt, calls rs_stay_in_table(lq_sta, false) and returns without changing the rate or turning on aggregation. If a search was in progress it adopts the search table when its throughput exceeds lq_sta->last_tpt, otherwise it reverts to the active table's rate and marks the uCode table for update; it then clears search_better_tbl, marks the search done and skips mode switching. Otherwise it picks an action with rs_get_rate_action (downscale to the adjacent lower rate, upscale to the higher, or stay, in which case rs_tpc_perform may request an update when staying in the column), but if the rate is MIMO and BT coex forbids MIMO it forces a search with rs_stay_in_table(lq_sta, true). If the rate changed it stores the new index, optionally tweaks the table, sets the A-MSDU length and sends the new rate table. It then calls rs_stay_in_table(lq_sta, false); if the rate did not change, no search just ended, the state is RS_STATE_SEARCH_CYCLE_STARTED and the window has counted packets it saves last_tpt and selects the next column to try (switching to it and setting search_better_tbl and programming the search table, or moving to RS_STATE_SEARCH_CYCLE_ENDED when no column is left). If ndp is false it calls rs_tl_turn_on_agg, and at the end, when a search is done and the state is SEARCH_CYCLE_ENDED, it sets the stay-in-table state.

name: iwl_mvm_pass_packet_to_mac80211
prose: Static helper in iwlwifi MVM rx.c (lines 45-94; the slice cut the head) that builds an skb from a received frame and passes it to mac80211. With hdrlen = ieee80211_hdrlen(hdr->frame_control) it calls skb_reserve(skb, hdrlen & 3) to align the later IP header. It then recomputes the number of bytes to copy: len if len <= skb_tailroom(skb) (after the reserve), otherwise hdrlen + crypt_len + 8. It appends that many bytes from hdr to the skb with skb_put_data (the caller must ensure the skb has room for them and that hdr is readable for them). If fraglen = len - copied bytes is non-zero it steals the rxb page with rxb_steal_page and adds it to the skb as fragment 0 at the offset of the rest of the frame within the page, with length fraglen and the rxb truesize. Finally it calls ieee80211_rx_napi(mvm->hw, sta, skb, napi), which takes ownership of the skb. It returns nothing.

name: iwl_mvm_add_sta
prose: Adds a station to the iwlwifi MVM driver and firmware (mvm/sta.c:1841-1910; the caller holds mvm->mutex; the slice cut the head). Outside a HW restart it picks a free station id with iwl_mvm_find_free_sta_id; during a restart it reuses mvm_sta->deflink.sta_id. In both cases it returns -ENOSPC if the id is IWL_INVALID_STA (so a stored invalid id during restart also gives -ENOSPC). It initialises the station spinlock. During a HW restart it first adds an empty internal station (iwl_mvm_add_int_sta_common, its error is returned), calls iwl_mvm_realloc_queues_after_restart (a void function, so no error from it) and requests an update to firmware (with STA_MODIFY_QUEUES unless the new TX API is used); otherwise it calls iwl_mvm_sta_init (error returned). It then calls iwl_mvm_sta_send_to_fw; on any error it returns the code and performs no rollback in this function, and the station is not published. On success, for a station vif it sets mvmvif->deflink.ap_sta_id = sta_id for a non-TDLS station (WARN_ON if it was already valid) or, for TDLS, only WARN_ONs that ap_sta_id is valid, publishes the station in mvm->fw_id_to_mac_id[sta_id] with rcu_assign_pointer and returns 0.

name: iwl_trans_pcie_removal_wk
prose: Work function (pcie/gen1_2/trans.c:2182-2267; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head) that removes an inaccessible iwlwifi PCIe device. wk is the work_struct embedded in a heap-allocated struct iwl_trans_pcie_removal (pdev, mode, integrated); the caller has taken a module reference and a pci_dev reference on pdev. It takes pci_lock_rescan_remove. If pdev->bus is NULL (something else already removed it) it goes straight to cleanup without any uevent, reset or removal and without calling pci_dev_put on pdev, so the pdev reference is not released on this path. Otherwise it emits a KOBJ_CHANGE uevent 'EVENT=INACCESSIBLE'. If mode is IWL_RESET_MODE_PROD_RESET it looks for the companion Bluetooth device: for a non-integrated device, function 1 of the same slot via pci_get_slot when pdev is function 0 (otherwise it logs 'Unexpected function'); for an integrated device by scanning all PCI devices on the same bus for one matching a list of Intel device ids; if found it logs, stops and removes it and drops its reference. It then calls iwl_trans_pcie_set_product_reset(pdev, mode == PROD_RESET, integrated), calls iwl_trans_pcie_call_reset(pdev) when mode >= IWL_RESET_MODE_FUNC_RESET, stops and removes pdev's bus device, drops the pdev reference with pci_dev_put, and when mode >= IWL_RESET_MODE_RESCAN rescans the parent bus (or the bus itself if it has no parent). On all paths it then releases pci_lock_rescan_remove, frees the removal structure and drops the module reference with module_put(THIS_MODULE).

name: iwl_trans_pcie_dump_data
prose: Collects a firmware-error dump for the iwlwifi PCIe transport into a newly allocated buffer (pcie/gen1_2/trans.c:3530-3681; the slice cut the head). It returns NULL if dump_mask is 0. It computes dump_rbs = (iwl_trans_is_fw_error(trans) and the device is not mq_rx_supported and the RB bit is set in dump_mask), then sizes the dump: the header; the host-command queue (TXCMD bit set and the command queue exists); the FW monitor (via iwl_trans_get_fw_monitor_len); CSR registers; FH registers (the gen2 or gen1 range); when dump_rbs is set, the closed receive buffers of rxq[0] (counted under rxq[0].lock with spin_lock_bh); and on gen2 with the PAGING bit set, each paging block. It then vzalloc's the buffer and returns NULL if that fails. It fills the sections selected by the mask in order: TXCMD (walking the command queue under cmdq->lock with spin_lock_bh, copying each non-empty command up to TFD_MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE bytes and passing it through sanitize_ops->frob_hcmd when provided), CSR, FH registers, RBs (only when dump_rbs), paging blocks (gen2 and PAGING bit), and the FW monitor. It stores the number of bytes written after the header in dump_data->len and returns the buffer, which the caller must release with vfree. It takes and releases the rxq[0] and command-queue locks itself.

name: iwl_trans_pcie_alloc
prose: Allocates and initialises the iwlwifi PCIe transport (pcie/gen1_2/trans.c:3747-3947; static; the slice cut the head). It allocates the iwl_trans (failure: ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM)), initialises the command wait queue and allocates the TX command pool (error: out_free_trans). It sets the TFD parameters for gen2 or gen1, the supported DMA mask and max skb frags, allocates the per-CPU TSO header pages (-ENOMEM: out_free_txcmd_pool) and computes the byte-count table size; only for gen2 devices does it create the byte-count DMA pool (-ENOMEM: out_free_tso). It allocates a dummy NAPI netdev (-ENOMEM: out_free_tso), initialises locks and wait queues, and creates the 'rb_allocator' workqueue (-ENOMEM: out_free_ndev). It may disable PCIe L0s/L1/CLKPM, sets a DMA mask of the TFD address size, falling back to 32 bits, and fails through out_no_pci if neither works; it writes the PCI retry-timeout config byte, disables interrupts, computes hw_rev_step, calls iwl_pcie_set_interrupt_capa and allocates the invalid-TX command buffer (error: out_no_pci). It then either sets up MSI-X handlers (error: out_no_pci) or allocates the ICT table and requests a shared threaded IRQ (ICT allocation error: out_no_pci; IRQ error: out_free_ict). On success it initialises debugfs monitor state and the debug TLV data and returns trans. The error labels run in a fall-through chain: out_free_ict frees the ICT, out_no_pci destroys the workqueue, out_free_ndev frees the NAPI netdev, out_free_tso frees the per-CPU pages, out_free_txcmd_pool destroys the command pool and out_free_trans frees the transport, then ERR_PTR(ret) is returned; the invalid-TX command buffer is not freed explicitly by these labels.

name: lbs_process_event
prose: Dispatches a firmware event for the libertas driver (real name lbs_process_event(priv, event), cmdresp.c:223-352; the slice shows only its second half; returns nothing). It switches on event: LINK_SENSED only logs; DEAUTHENTICATED and DISASSOCIATED call lbs_mac_event_disconnected(priv, false) and LINK_LOST_NO_SCAN calls it with true; PS_SLEEP does nothing if psstate is PS_STATE_FULL_POWER or if commands are pending in cmdpendingq, otherwise sets psstate to PS_STATE_PRE_SLEEP and calls lbs_ps_confirm_sleep; HOST_AWAKE calls priv->reset_deep_sleep_wakeup if set, clears is_deep_sleep, sends CMD_802_11_WAKEUP_CONFIRM with lbs_cmd_async using a local struct cmd_header that this function does not initialise, clears is_host_sleep_activated and wakes host_sleep_q; DEEP_SLEEP_AWAKE calls reset_deep_sleep_wakeup if set, clears is_deep_sleep and wakes ds_awake_q; PS_AWAKE is ignored in FULL_POWER, otherwise sets psstate to PS_STATE_AWAKE and, if needtowakeup is set, calls lbs_set_ps_mode(priv, PS_MODE_ACTION_EXIT_PS, false); MIC_ERR_UNICAST and MIC_ERR_MULTICAST call lbs_send_mic_failureevent; MIB_CHANGED, INIT_DONE, ADHOC_BCN_LOST, and the RSSI/SNR/MAX_FAIL events only log (the last group with netdev_alert); MESH_AUTO_STARTED logs and is ignored; any other event logs an 'unknown event id' alert.

name: capability_store
prose: sysfs store callback for the libertas mesh 'capability' attribute (mesh.c:757-790; static; the slice cut the head). It zeroes a local cmd_ds_mesh_config and parses buf with sscanf("%d") into datum, which is a uint32_t. It returns -EINVAL without further effect if sscanf does not return 1 or if datum is greater than 255; because the comparison is unsigned, a negative input also becomes a large value and is rejected. It then calls mesh_get_default_parameters(dev, &defs) and ignores its return value (so if that call fails, defs may be used without having been filled in), sets cmd.length to the size of struct mrvl_meshie, copies defs.meshie into the command data, overwrites mesh_capability of that copy with datum and sends the command with lbs_mesh_config_send(priv, &cmd, CMD_ACT_MESH_CONFIG_SET, CMD_TYPE_MESH_SET_MESH_IE). If the send returns a non-zero value that value is returned; otherwise it returns strlen(buf) (not count).

name: mwifiex_cfg80211_authenticate
prose: cfg80211 authenticate callback of mwifiex (real name mwifiex_cfg80211_authenticate, cfg80211.c:4265-4425; the slice shows only its tail, which is not mwifiex_cfg80211_mgmt_tx). It returns -EFAULT if the interface role is UAP, -EINVAL if the wdev type is not STATION, and -EBUSY if an auth is pending (HOST_MLME_AUTH_PENDING) while the current auth algorithm is not SAE. It registers the host-MLME management-frame mask with the firmware on first use, maps req->auth_type to an auth algorithm (open, shared key, FT, LEAP or SAE; any other type returns -EOPNOTSUPP), and, if no auth is pending, sets a remain-on-channel on the BSS channel (failure: -EFAULT; success: stores a random cookie and the channel in priv->roc_cfg). It stores the authentication mode, cancels scans, computes the frame length (ie_len + auth_data_len + header and auth body lengths, minus 4 when auth_data_len >= 4) and returns -EINVAL if it exceeds U16_MAX and -ENOMEM if the skb allocation fails. It then fills the skb's tx_info (bss_num, bss_type, pkt_len), reserves and pushes the packet length, tx_control and pkt_type, builds an authentication management frame (da and bssid from req->bss->bssid, sa from priv->curr_addr, broadcast addr4); when auth_data_len >= 4 it takes the transaction number and status code from the first four bytes of auth_data only for SAE and copies auth_data + 4 (auth_data_len - 4 bytes) into the variable part, then sets auth_alg, auth_transaction (default 1) and status_code (default 0), and appends req->ie (ie_len bytes) after the auth data. It sets priv->auth_flag = HOST_MLME_AUTH_PENDING and priv->auth_alg, sets the skb priority to WMM_HIGHEST_PRIORITY, timestamps it, passes it to mwifiex_queue_tx_pkt (which takes ownership) and returns 0.

name: mwifiex_send_rgpower_table
prose: Parses a regulatory-power table text and sends it to the firmware as host commands (real name mwifiex_send_rgpower_table(priv, data, size), sta_cmd.c:1509-1597; the slice shows only the second part of it). It allocates a zeroed mwifiex_ds_misc_cmd and a copy of data (-ENOMEM if either allocation fails; both are freed automatically on return). It loops while the position is inside the copy: it first calls mwifiex_rgpower_table_advance_to_content, which skips whitespace, NULs and '#' comment lines (it returns -EINVAL if a comment has no terminating newline), and that error is returned. When it sees '}' while inside a command block it sets hostcmd->len from the 16-bit little-endian value at cmd[2], sends it with mwifiex_send_cmd (a failure is returned), clears the command buffer and starts over. Outside a block it looks for '=' and then '{' to start a block, and returns -EINVAL ('syntax error in hostcmd') if either is missing. Inside a block it splits the line on spaces and converts each token with kstrtou8(token, 16) into the command buffer; a hex parse error is returned, and -ENOMEM is returned if the command would exceed MWIFIEX_SIZE_OF_CMD_BUFFER. When the whole text has been consumed it returns 0 (a block that was opened but not closed with '}' is not sent).

prose: Handles a firmware event for a station-mode mwifiex interface (real name mwifiex_process_sta_event(priv), sta_event.c:696-1098; the slice shows only the last part of its switch; returns int, initially 0). The CHANNEL_SWITCH_ANN case also sets priv->csa_expire_time and priv->csa_chan. TX_DATA_PAUSE, MULTI_CHAN_INFO, TX_STATUS_REPORT, BT_COEX_WLAN_PARA_CHANGE (ignored when ignore_btcoex_events is set), RXBA_SYNC, FW_DUMP_INFO and UNKNOWN_DEBUG call void helpers or only log.
